newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures cut losses, most still soft.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures cut losses, most still soft.

text.p: IMM currency futures cut opening losses and visited morning peaks after U.S. data, but most lacked upside followthrough in early trading.
Futures edged up to highs as U.S. Treasury bond futures wobbled up then back down when a report on retail-level inflation last month showed scant upward pressure.
Consumer prices rose 0.2 percent overall and in the core rate, as forecast. June's 0.1-percent gains remained the same.
Weekly jobless claims also meshed closely with forecasts, rising to 316,000 from an upwardly revised 304,000 and against expectations for 317,000.
"They all on target," said Mike Malpede, foreign exchange analyst, Refco Inc, of the initial barrage of economic data.
July U.S. industrial output subsequently was reported up 0.2 percent, as forecast, with capacity use dipping to 83.1 percent rate compared to forecasts for 83.5 percent rate.
Those data elicited little initial response in currencies, although futures then pulled back toward day's lows as U.S. T-bond futures floated back up toward the morning's peaks.
Instead, brokers said focus stuck on crosses, technicals and interest-rate differentials, with EMU concerns continuing to hover in and out of the spotlight.
"The D-mark seems to be continuing to rise against the yen on that cross," said one currency futures floor broker.

Brokers said sentiment the Bundesbank might be priming the market for a rate hike, especially after Wednesday's monthly report highlighted German inflation concerns, persisted and could cushion the mark against the dollar as well.
"I think a lot of it is the idea we are at the end of the rate-hike cycle," said the floor broker of U.S. and U.K. interest rate. He also said German rates are expected to rise before Japanese rates.

Currencies subsequently eroded and revisited or pierced their overnight lows, however, as the dollar surmounted technical resistance near 117.00 yen, which roughly corresponds to $0.008585 in September yen futures.
Futures floor brokers noted talk that a fund sold about 2,000 September yen starting near $0.008600, with sellstops triggered at about $0.008590.

At 0940 CDT/1440 GMT, Sept yen off $0.000160 at $0.008527, marks off $0.0031 to $0.5429, Swiss fr off $0.0054 at $0.6589, pound up $0.0032 at $1.5852, Cdollar up $0.0009 at $0.7200, A.dollar fell $0.0011 to $0.7433, Mex peso up $0.000350 to $0.127150.
